citations.quote: A graphic circulating online claims that the judges assigned to former president Rodrigo Duterte’s case in the International Criminal Court have rejected the evidence and moved to end his trial.
The ICC has denied this and reiterated that the trial will push through, with the opening still scheduled for Nov. 30.
The graphic bore the text: “UPDATE FROM THE HAGUE. GOOD NEWS! MAJORITY OF ICC JUDGES REJECT THE EVIDENCE AND MOVE TO END THE TRIAL BEFORE THE YEAR ENDS.”

The post also read: “UPDATE FROM THE HAGUE. A developing update is drawing attention: reports circulating online claim that a majority of ICC judges may reject key evidence and could move toward ending the trial before the year ends. What happens next could have major implications. Stay informed, follow verified developments, and wait for official court announcements before drawing conclusions. For updates, facts, and the latest developments—stay tuned. #ICC #TheHague #Philippines #Justice #Duterte.”
In a Sept. 11 email to VERA Files, the ICC’s Public Affairs Unit disowned the circulating claims.

“Contrary to what these social media posts say, the opening of the trial is still scheduled for 30 November, and the Chamber will hold a hearing next week on 16 September to discuss preparations for the trial,” a portion of the email said.

"It really is important, even more important than normal, that we conclude the case as quickly as possible," she said.

Korner said the chamber intends to sit continuously, from November 30 until the week before the Christmas break and then from January until the Easter break, instead of in blocks separated by breaks as the Registry proposed.

citations.quote: The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III on Wednesday set the opening of the trial of former President Rodrigo Duterte’s crime against humanity case over his war on illegal drugs during his time as President and Davao City mayor on November 30, 2026.

“The start of trial, we are prepared to accede to the prosecution’s application of the 30th of November as the start of trial,” Presiding Judge Joanna Korner said during the case’s first status conference.
According to Korner, the trial will run daily until a judicial recess.

During the conference, Korner said the ICC prosecution wants to begin Duterte’s trial on November 30 while Duterte’s defense team did not want to propose a date until matters regarding his fitness were resolved.
